title: Reproduction in flowering plants
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:53Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point covers the same pollination, fertilisation and fruit idea but is broader, adding asexual reproduction with runners and bulbs and a question on it, which the new point does not ask for, and removing that material would be more than a small change.

draft.title: Reproduction in flowering plants
card: the part that makes pollen. Pollen holds the male sex cells.
the sticky top of the female part, which catches pollen. Wind or animals such as bees carry pollen from an anther to a stigma. This is called pollination.
the part at the base of the female part, which holds the ovules. Ovules contain the female sex cells. Fertilisation happens here when a male cell joins an ovule's egg cell.
Each fertilised ovule becomes a seed. The ovary around the seeds grows into the fruit.
draft.remember: Pollen goes from anther to stigma, then fertilisation in the ovary makes seeds, and the ovary becomes the fruit.

a.q: After fertilisation in a flower, what does the ovary become?
opts: The fruit, which surrounds the seeds
The seed, which holds the new plant
The pollen, which carries male cells
a.why: The fertilised ovules become seeds, and the ovary around them grows into the fruit. The seed is tempting, but it develops from the ovule, not from the whole ovary.
a.clue: Think about what surrounds the seeds in a tomato.

b.q: Mia sees a bee carry yellow dust from one wattle flower to another. Where must the dust land for fertilisation to follow?
opts: On the stigma, so the male cells can reach the ovary
On the anther, so the male cells can reach the ovary
On the ovary wall, so the stigma can make seeds
On the stigma, so the anther can make new pollen
b.why: The yellow dust is pollen, and it must land on the stigma. From there the male cells reach the ovules in the ovary, where fertilisation happens. The anther is tempting, but it makes pollen rather than catching it.
b.clue: Which part is sticky and catches pollen?

wants.brief: A labelled cross-section of a flower showing the anther, stigma and ovary with an ovule inside it, using the same names as the card.
wants.why: Seeing where each part sits helps the student follow pollen from anther to stigma and then to the ovary.

a.best: The fruit, which surrounds the seeds

b.best: On the stigma, so the male cells can reach the ovary
